source_text:
56 ∆εῖ δὲ φιλαλήθως τοὺς ἐννόμους ἀγωνιστὰς πάντα συμπεριλαβόντας ἀπαραλείπτως, ἀλλὰ μὴ πρὸς ἀπάτην μέρος μὲν ἀποσιωπᾶν, μέρος δὲ ἀποσπῶντας
προφέρειν. 57 Εἰ γὰρ κτιστὸς οὐκ ἄρα γεννητός· εἰ δὲ γεννητὸς, οὐ κτιστός· ἐπεὶ μηδὲ οἷόν τε περὶ τὴν αὐτὴν φύσιν ἑκάτερον στρέφεσθαι τὸ γένος. 58 Πᾶν τὸ ἀρχὴν ἔχον καὶ τέλος ἐπιδέχεται, πᾶν τὸ τέλος ἐπιδεχόμενον φθορᾶς ἐστιν δεκτικόν.
thought_title: Lawful contenders must not mutilate; created and begotten exclude each other; what has a beginning admits corruption
orientation: Eustathius is concluding his refutation of the Arians, first stating the rule for honest use of Scripture, then arguing that 'created' and 'begotten' cannot both apply to Christ, and finally that whatever has a beginning is capable of corruption.
pass_a_gloss: But it is necessary that lawful contenders who love the truth embrace all things without omission, not silence one part for deception while tearing away another part to present it. For if created, then not begotten; but if begotten, not created; since it is not even possible for each kind to apply to the same nature. Everything having a beginning also admits an end; everything admitting an end is capable of corruption.

choices.why: Adverbial form preserved to keep the manner of the contenders' action explicit, matching the compound's literal sense.
Keeps the legal-contest metaphor from the previous section (false accusers, prosecutors) and the adjective's force of 'within the law.'
Renders the double emphasis on completeness: the compound verb 'embracing together' plus the adverb 'without omission.'

choices.term: μέρος μὲν ἀποσιωπᾶν, μέρος δὲ ἀποσπῶντας προφέρειν
choices.english: silence one part and tear away another part to present it
choices.why: Preserves the μέν...δέ contrast and the violent verb ἀποσπῶντας ('tearing away'), which echoes the mutilation imagery of the previous section.
rejected: keep silent about one part and bring forward another part
suppress one part and produce another part

choices.why: The middle voice suggests the two categories cannot turn or circulate around the same nature; 'revolve' keeps the spatial metaphor.
Matches the glossary rendering for φθορᾶς δεκτικόν, keeping the noun 'corruption' rather than an adjective.

pass_b_english: Lawful contenders who love the truth must embrace all things without omission, not silence one part and tear away another part to present it for deception. For if Christ is created, then he is not begotten; and if he is begotten, then he is not created, since both categories cannot revolve around the same nature. Everything that has a beginning also admits an end, and everything that admits an end is capable of corruption.
